data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Academic peer review is centrally gated by editors assigning manuscripts, whereas DeepReason's schools are decentralized conditioning-only schools.","Peer review aims for individual manuscript acceptance or rejection, while DeepReason aims for the global retirement of rival theoretical positions."],"overturn_conditions":["DeepReason's system possesses an unmodeled garbage collector that automatically retires rival positions when their coverage debt exceeds a threshold.","The per-target warrant graph is sparse and structured rather than combinatorial, preventing the batch criticism backlog explosion."],"shared_structure":["Both involve a bounded resource (criticism-weighted attention capacity / reviewer time) processing a combinatorially growing workload (per-target warrants / manuscript reviews).","Both can enter a backlog state where throughput drops to near zero as the number of active items grows, trapping the system in an unproductive attractor."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_007","SRC_008"],"transfer_claims":["DeepReason could adopt a 'desk-reject' triage mechanism to filter out low-coverage rival positions before they enter the full per-target warrant queue, mimicking editorial triage to reduce coverage debt."]},"claim":"The near-zero retirement rate of rival positions is caused by a coverage debt explosion in the batch criticism mechanism, where the combinatorial growth of per-target warrants outpaces the criticism-weighted attention budget, trapping the system in a high-rivalry, low-retirement attractor. A sandboxed Python simulation (sandboxed_python_v1) should model this by varying the batch size and attention cap to predict whether coverage debt grows as O(N^2) or O(N log N) with the number of rival positions N, testing if a triage mechanism can restore retirement.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The coverage debt mechanism has a hidden decay rate that keeps the backlog bounded, preventing the attractor.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The criticism-weighted attention budget scales dynamically with the number of accepted rival positions, avoiding the combinatorial bottleneck.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Rival positions are inherently independent, so batch criticism does not require per-target warrants across all pairs, limiting the combinatorial explosion.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"As described in block f1e4808bfe8d (SRC_001), budget-pressure creates a selection loop. In batch criticism, each new rival position requires per-target warrants against existing rivals. If attention is criticism-weighted but capped, the capacity per warrant drops as N grows (from 18 to 60), causing coverage debt to accumulate faster than it can be retired. This aligns with block 10aba4af94908 (SRC_008), showing the machine's current holdings are accumulating without being retired, leading to the isolation and degenerate lineage described in block 78d2ed4cd3ea7 (SRC_007). The system's inability to retire rivals despite generating them violates the normative amendments expected in block 0c2615387971a (SRC_004).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
